name: Newport Beach
intro: Newport Beach is where we are based and where most of our work has been, from the peninsula to the bluffs above the harbor.

Building here means working close to the water: tight lots, neighbors on every side, and much of the city inside the California coastal zone, where many projects need a coastal development permit as well as a building permit.

considerations.title: Coastal zone permitting
considerations.body: Much of Newport Beach lies within the coastal zone. Depending on the property and scope, a project may need a coastal development permit in addition to a building permit, which affects schedule.

considerations.title: Tight lots and access
considerations.body: Narrow lots, alleys and shared walls make staging, deliveries and concrete pours a planning exercise of their own.

considerations.title: Building near salt air
considerations.body: Material and detailing choices matter more near the ocean. We talk them through during budgeting, not after.

name: Newport Coast
intro: Newport Coast is hillside country: larger custom homes on graded lots, with long views over the Pacific.
Many Newport Coast homes sit within master-planned communities, so in addition to the city, an association's architectural review is often part of getting a project approved.

considerations.title: Association review
considerations.body: Community associations commonly review plans before construction. We build that step into the schedule from the start.

considerations.title: Hillside foundations
considerations.body: Sloped lots put more of the budget into the ground. Doing our own structural concrete keeps that work under our direct control.

considerations.title: Large-scale custom homes
considerations.body: Bigger homes mean more trades, more coordination and more to track. Weekly meetings and job documentation keep it visible.

name: Corona del Mar
intro: Corona del Mar is a village within the City of Newport Beach, with small lots, walkable streets and homes that step down toward the beaches and the bluffs.
Projects here are often about getting the most out of a modest footprint: careful planning, efficient structure and a construction site that respects a close-knit street.

considerations.title: Small-footprint planning
considerations.body: On compact lots every foot counts. We review plans early for structure and cost so the space goes where it matters.

considerations.title: City of Newport Beach process
considerations.body: Corona del Mar projects go through the City of Newport Beach, and coastal zone rules can apply depending on location.

considerations.title: Being a good neighbor
considerations.body: Narrow streets mean planned deliveries, tidy staging and clear communication with the people next door.

name: Costa Mesa
intro: Costa Mesa sits just inland of Newport Beach, with a mix of established neighborhoods and lots that often have room to grow.
That room is why many Costa Mesa homeowners look at additions, remodels and accessory dwelling units, and why a clear budget before design is so useful.

considerations.title: ADUs and additions
considerations.body: Lot sizes in many Costa Mesa neighborhoods can make ADUs and additions practical. We start with what the lot and city rules allow.

considerations.title: City of Costa Mesa permitting
considerations.body: Costa Mesa has its own building and planning process. We help prepare the submittal and respond to plan-check comments.

considerations.title: Working with what's there
considerations.body: Older homes can hide surprises. Plan review and an honest budget contingency keep them from becoming emergencies.

name: Huntington Beach
intro: Huntington Beach stretches from inland neighborhoods to the harbor and the open coast, with everything from tract-home remodels to new custom homes near the water.
Whichever end of the city a project is in, the same fundamentals apply: a realistic budget, buildable plans, and a structure built right the first time.

considerations.title: Coastal and inland sites
considerations.body: Properties near the beach or harbor can fall within the coastal zone, which can add permit steps. Inland properties usually follow the standard city process.

considerations.title: City of Huntington Beach permitting
considerations.body: Projects go through the City of Huntington Beach. We help assemble the submittal and work through plan check.

considerations.title: Remodel or rebuild
considerations.body: For many older homes, the first question is whether to remodel or rebuild. Quantity take-offs and a clear budget help answer it.
